parsed.explanation: The combined regime is high risk because federal entry screening, sex-marker document rules, federal single-sex facility policy, and immigration/federal custody carry severe visitor-facing harm. State/province protections reduce local daily exposure: non-discrimination, public accommodation, corrected IDs, insurer care mandates, hate-crime recourse, and state custody protections. No local violence pattern is documented. Families with trans minors add national child-care and school enforcement hostility, though state law shields care. The gate remains federal, so local remedies cannot assure safety if outed at border or federal site.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal sex-marker policy requires M/F, blocks nonmatching passports/visas; officers may refuse when records mismatch and consider permanent ineligibility if fraud. Travelers report passports blocked/confiscated and stranded; allied advisories document visitor exposure.
entry_documents.protection: Existing nonmatching passports remain valid; national litigation and legal-aid guidance exist; state IDs and anti-discrimination may ease local services but do not change federal entry.
entry_documents.interaction: State document protections cannot offset border screening; any mismatch may trigger federal review rather than local correction.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal/immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse; national corrections adopted conversion-therapy policies; birth-sex placement is plausible.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State law protects incarcerated transgender people in state custody, but not immigration/federal facilities.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document or visa suspicion can escalate into federal custody; state custody protections do not apply there.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities by identity; federal facilities impose birth-sex constraints; some states criminalize use.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State public accommodation anti-discrimination and no documented state ban; private/state facilities likely less exposed if local law is enforced.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federally controlled or funded facilities can override state protections during airport, immigration, and federal-building encounters.

care_services.exposure: Federal hostility to gender-affirming care, especially minors, includes reimbursement blocks, funding threats, records subpoenas, and youth-care restrictions upheld.
care_services.protection: State insurers and public programme mandated to cover medically necessary care; insurer discrimination prohibited; state provider protections exist.
care_services.interaction: Adult private/local care is safer; minors and guardians are more exposed where federal rules or public insurance touch care.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal executive and counterterrorism language frames radical pro-transgender ideology, directs school enforcement, and rewards investigations tied to law violations; increases profiling and hostile discretion.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime law and state constitutional equality/hate-crime reporting provide recourse; some federal orders are blocked or enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State protections reduce local harassment, but federal officers can still enforce hostile national policy at gates and federal sites.

minors_guardians.exposure: For guardians travelling with a trans minor, federal orders criminalize facilitating social transition, target schools/care, restrict youth care, and records checks can out the child.
minors_guardians.protection: State anti-bullying law, school sports policy reversal, insurer coverage mandates, and care/custody statutes support minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardians may need state insurers and local settings to avoid federal exposure; family status does not prevent federal screening.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No dated state/province incident pattern is documented; national bias violence is possible and advisories say check reports. Absence of evidence is not safety.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State non-discrimination, hate-crime reporting, constitutional equality, and low-risk assessment; local police likely responsive under state law.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street friction handled locally may be mitigated; federal encounters may be handled under hostile national policy.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Federal litigation over passports and orders is unresolved; facility map lacks this state entry; healthcare-equity and incarcerated-protection gaps are qualitative; enforcement varies by officer and facility.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties suit, legal-aid FAQ, courts, state complaint mechanisms, and hate-crime hotline offer partial recourse.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies may soften local harms but cannot assure safe federal gate handling; uncertainty keeps risk elevated.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similarity: federal document discrepancy can trigger investigation and custody harms can be severe. Difference: this protective division lacks routine arrest for presentation, has state non-discrimination/care/custody law, and courts/legal aid intervene; higher than 0.15-D.

Both impose visitor-facing border denial or stranding from gender-marker mismatch. This case is less arbitrary locally because state protections apply, but possible federal immigration custody and child-care hostility keep it near or slightly above 0.35-A.

0.75-C has respectful border treatment, marker recognition, brief detention, and reliable remedies. This case lacks federal recognition and includes birth-sex custody and care hostility, so it is materially lower despite strong state protections.

parsed.synthesis: Operationally, a visitor is screened by national binary-document and birth-sex facility rules before state protections matter. If documents match presentation enough and the traveller remains in state/private settings, local anti-discrimination, care mandates, and state custody law can be significant shields. The danger concentrates at borders, federal sites, immigration custody, and minor/guardian care disputes. Unresolved litigation and inconsistent enforcement prevent recovery to Reduced Risk.
